editorial.headline: Technical Certification Is Open Nationally and Not Moratorium-Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers certification across products, processes, services and management systems, with full national foreign ownership and no Bali moratorium block recorded.
editorial.body:
Technical certification is the business of assessing and certifying products, processes, services and systems. Its remit reaches well beyond a single industry: the recorded scope includes certification for quality, environmental and food-safety management systems; HACCP; energy management; medical-device management; supply-chain security; laboratory biorisk; anti-bribery; information-technology services; compliance; sustainable events; tourism; ecolabels; occupational safety and health; organic systems; forestry and timber legality; ISPO; halal products; green industry; construction services and warehouses. In practical terms, this is an assurance activity whose subject may be an organisation’s system, a commercial service, a product standard or a defined operational process.

The code is open across the full recorded business-scale range: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That matters because certification is not framed here as an activity reserved for one size of enterprise. The national position is equally clear: it is TERBUKA to foreign investment, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. The applicable national reference recorded for that position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.

Bali does not reverse that national openness in this record. The provincial rule blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk activities, island-wide and permanently. This activity is not recorded as blocked by that moratorium. At the Besar scale, its OSS risk is recorded as Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, which places it outside the moratorium’s stated Low and Medium-Low risk boundary. The Bali status is therefore recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK: the relevant point is not that Bali creates a separate foreign-ownership cap, but that the activity is not caught by the province-wide PMA moratorium on the lower-risk categories.

For a founder, the distinction is worth holding precisely. Nationally, the activity permits up to 100% foreign ownership. In Bali, the record does not show a moratorium prohibition for it; rather, it identifies a higher risk classification at the Besar scale. That is the honest picture supplied by the record: an open technical-certification activity, available across all listed scales, whose Bali position remains outside the permanent restriction aimed at Low and Medium-Low risk activities.
editorial.pullQuote: In Bali, this activity is not caught by the province-wide PMA moratorium because its recorded Besar-scale risk sits above the restricted categories.
